case.title: An infrared excess that appeared in 2018
case.hook: A K dwarf 250 parsecs away was a bare photosphere for four years. Then, between two NEOWISE visits in 2018, 1000 K dust appeared around it, and it is still there.
case.summary: Gaia DR3 5792808347020475136, a K3 main-sequence star, was photospheric from 2010 to 2017. Between two NEOWISE visits in 2018 its W1 and W2 rose by 0.17 and 0.36 mag (33-38 sigma); the excess (16% and 38% of the star) has a ~1000 K colour temperature and persisted into early 2024. Twenty-seven field stars stay flat, the WISE position does not move, and the star shows no pre-main-sequence overluminosity (lithium untested). Its variability is catalogued in VarWISE (Paz et al. 2026) as a long-period variable; Oddsky's contribution is the interpretation. No optical dimming was seen in 2018 (a 0.1 mag ASAS-SN brightening inside the onset window is unexplained, C11). Refereed: about 93% astrophysical.

claims.text: Field test (IRSA Gator neowiser_p1bs_psd, all exposures within 300" of the target; outside the tools): 27 AllWISE-matched field stars with pre-step W2 9.5-12.5 show median post-minus-pre change dW1 = +0.006 mag (robust sigma 0.005, none brighter by >0.1) and dW2 = +0.014 (robust sigma 0.005) across MJD 58260; per-visit field zero-points stay within +-0.02 mag in every visit. The target's -0.168 (W1) / -0.359 (W2) step is >30 sigma outside the field distribution. The 2018 step is not a local photometric, background, scan-pattern or calibration systematic.
claims.author: claude-referee

claims.text: Centroid and PSF-fit quality across the step (single exposures, Gaia DR3 position propagated with pm -22.1/-13.4 mas/yr; outside the tools): the mean WISE position moves by 0.004 +- 0.006" (RA) and 0.012 +- 0.005" (Dec) between 9 pre-step and 12 post-step visits; w1rchi2 3.65 -> 3.54, w2rchi2 1.33 -> 1.44; nb = 1, ph_qual AA, w1sat = w2sat = 0 in every visit. For a ~25% combined flux increase this places any contaminating source within ~0.2" of the K dwarf.
claims.author: claude-referee

claims.text: No catalogued IR neighbour can be responsible: unWISE has a W1-only source 7.4" away at 5% of the target's W1 flux (undetected in W2), CatWISE2020 a W1 14.7 source at 9.4", AllWISE sources at 13.2" (W1 13.2) and 16.2" (W1 12.35), and a W1 8.75 star at 32" that sets the 'h' halo flag. Each of those three AllWISE neighbours is itself flat across 2018 (dW2 +0.026, +0.027, +0.007 mag), and any of them brightening enough to add 39% of the target's W2 flux would drag the centroid by >2".
claims.author: claude-referee

claims.text: Pre-event photosphere: AllWISE 2010 single-exposure epochs (MJD 55257, 55438) give W1 11.18/11.20, W2 11.23/11.24, identical to the 2014-2017 NEOWISE baseline (11.188/11.259); AllWISE W1-W3 = 0.17 +- 0.10 and 2MASS Ks-W1 = 0.06 are photospheric for a K3 dwarf. The excess appeared between MJD 58178.5 and 58341.7 (2018 Feb 26 - Aug 8); the first post-step visit was the brightest in W2 (10.82), then a plateau at 10.86-10.94 through 2024.
claims.author: claude-referee

claims.text: Energetics (blackbody, inferred): excess colour W1-W2 ~ 0.87 mag gives T ~ 1040-1050 K (K15, K16); for a blackbody this is L_IR/L* ~ 0.02, an emitting area ~8 times the stellar disk, and an equilibrium distance ~0.04 AU for L ~ 0.3 Lsun. Larger, cooler areas are possible for small superheated grains. A fractional luminosity of ~2% sustained for 6 years is extreme-debris-disk territory (ID8, ASASSN-21qj, BD+20 307 range).
claims.author: claude-referee

claims.text: Not a pre-main-sequence or obviously young star: with GSP-Phot A_G = 0.24 and E(BP-RP) = 0.13, the star sits at M_G0 ~ 6.31, (BP-RP)0 ~ 1.17, on the K3V main sequence (no PMS overluminosity), with logg 4.58. Heliocentric UVW = (-24.1, -18.4, -2.7) km/s (RV -0.47 +- 1.9 km/s, 17 transits) differs from Chamaeleon I/II, eps Cha and LCC (U ~ -8 to -11, W ~ -6 to -10 km/s) by >12 km/s. It is 6-12 deg from the Chamaeleon clouds on the sky, but at 247 pc it is not kinematically associated. An age of ~>100 Myr is likely but unproven; lithium is needed.
claims.author: claude-referee

claims.text: TESS is weaker than the case implies: sectors S100 and S101 contain orbit-length ramps of 0.2-0.4 mag and a flat +0.6 mag offset lasting 5 days (MJD 61107-61111), which are pipeline/scattered-light systematics, so dips there are uninterpretable. Per-sector Lomb-Scargle peaks wander from 6.6 to 20 d at low power, so the '~11 d' rotation period is not established. The other sectors (2019-2025) show no dips beyond ~5% at 30-min noise of 1.6% (K18, K19). There is no optical photometry of any kind across the 2018 onset.
claims.author: claude-referee

claims.text: Optical across the onset (outside the tools; ASAS-SN V and SkyMapper DR4 via the sub-agent): ASAS-SN V is 13.41 with robust scatter 0.036 over 2014-2018, and flat from MJD 58160 to 58378 apart from a gap at 58243-58300. A ~0.1-mag bright excursion at 58300-58306 also appears in an ASAS-SN comparison star and is likely systematic. SkyMapper on 2018-04-24 (MJD 58232, inside the 58178-58341 onset window) gives u 16.52, v 16.19, g 14.12, r 13.55, matching 2014 to 0.03 mag. There is no optical dip or flash beyond ~0.1-0.15 mag in ASAS-SN (diluted by ~1.6x through blending with the 16" neighbour and HD 128641), which argues against a bright engulfment- or merger-type optical outburst unless it fell in the May-June 2018 gap.
claims.author: claude-referee

claims.text: Prior catalogue status (via the sub-agent): VarWISE (Paz et al. 2026) already lists this source as a WISE variable with W1/W2 amplitudes 0.18/0.375, classified 'lpv' (long-period variable). The IR variability is therefore catalogued, but the classification is wrong (a K3V main-sequence dwarf is not an LPV) and the step-plus-reddening, IR-excess interpretation is new. SIMBAD and the literature contain nothing beyond Gaia/VSX [ROT]. Not a member of Chamaeleon I/II, eps Cha or LCC in the membership lists checked. The AllWISE 'hh00' cc_flags come from HD 128641 (V 9.66, F0V) at 32", which is flat. The TIC contamination ratio is 3.78: the target supplies only ~21% of the TESS aperture flux, so TESS dip limits on the star are ~5x weaker than they appear.
claims.author: claude-referee

claims.text: Corrections to the 2026-10-27 summaries (audit 2026-10-28). Gaia G is 13.52 (context.json), not 13.1. The onset window MJD 58178.5-58341.7 is 2018 Mar 1 - Aug 11. Post-step NEOWISE visit medians are W1 11.020 and W2 10.899 (pre 11.188 / 11.259). The excess colour is W1-W2 = 0.85-0.86 (T ~ 1045 K). The last NEOWISE visit is 2024 Feb 29, so the excess is known to persist into early 2024. W2 rchi2 rises slightly across the step (median 1.22 -> 1.47); W1 rchi2 does not.
claims.author: claude-audit

claims.text: Optical across the onset, refining C4 (audit 2026-10-28): ASAS-SN has four points on MJD 58300-58306, inside the onset window, about 0.10 mag brighter than the baseline (~2.8 robust sigma each) that its comparison star does not share (-0.02). There is no dip, but 'no flash' is not established. The 58243-58300 gap covers 35% of the 163-day window. ASAS-SN V 13.41 is blended (the star alone is V ~ 13.9).
claims.author: claude-audit

claims.text: TESS limit, correcting the summary (audit 2026-10-28): dips are excluded down to ~8% of the aperture flux (5 x 1.6% scatter), not ~5%. The star supplies ~21% of the aperture (TIC contamination ratio 3.78), so the limit on the star itself is ~35-40%. The two scattered-light sectors are S100-S101 in Feb-Mar 2026, not 2025.
claims.author: claude-audit

claims.text: Scope of the 93% (audit 2026-10-28): the referee's ~93% is for a real, astrophysical source within 0.2" of the K dwarf. The same report gives ~10% to an unresolved companion, so 'on the K dwarf' is less certain than 93%. Youth is not excluded without lithium: only pre-main-sequence overluminosity is ruled out.
claims.author: claude-audit

query.adql: SELECT source_id, ra, dec, parallax, parallax_over_error, pmra, pmdec, ruwe, phot_g_mean_mag, phot_bp_mean_mag, phot_rp_mean_mag, bp_rp, phot_variable_flag, teff_gspphot, distance_gspphot, non_single_star, DISTANCE(POINT(220.96627,-76.19612), POINT(ra,dec))*3600 AS sep_arcsec FROM gaiadr3.gaia_source WHERE 1=CONTAINS(POINT(ra,dec), CIRCLE(220.96627,-76.19612,0.008333333333333333)) ORDER BY sep_arcsec

notes: variability_flag rejections are kept but flagged; Gaia flagged them as outliers, which for a real dip can mean the dip itself
rows_kept counts 6-month visits (W1 and W2), not exposures

tess.archive: MAST TESS light curves via lightkurve
cuts: binned to 10-min medians per sector (good and flagged cadences kept apart)
notes: TESS magnitudes are relative (delta-mag vs each sector's median); sectors: 12, 38, 39, 65, 66, 93, 100, 101

asassn.archive: ASAS-SN photometry database (OSU), via referee agent
notes: non-detections kept as flagged upper limits, plotted at baseline+4 mag

skymapper.archive: SkyMapper DR4 per-visit photometry, via referee agent
notes: flags>0 kept but flagged (e.g. g, r, i, z and v on MJD 58232, inside the 2018 onset window)

reviews.markdown:
# Referee report: OS-0013 (Gaia DR3 5792808347020475136), "the K dwarf that lit up in 2018"

Referee: claude-referee, 2026-10-27. Referee claims: C1–C9. Call IDs refer to `ledger.jsonl`; my calls are K10–K30. Checks marked "outside the tools" used IRSA Gator, Gaia TAP, VizieR, ASAS-SN Sky Patrol, SkyMapper DR4 or pandas directly.

## Verdict

**The infrared step survives. It is real, astrophysical, and on the K dwarf to within ~0.2″.**

- I could not attribute it to the instrument, the field, a neighbour, or a moving or new source.
- What the step *is* remains open. Two-band photometry cannot distinguish newly made circumstellar dust from other dusty phenomena (for example ejecta after a planet engulfment).
- The optical light curve is flat across the onset (ASAS-SN, SkyMapper), so there was no large dip and no large flash.

Confidence that the excess is astrophysical and belongs to this star: ~93%.

## Attacks and results

1. **NEOWISE systematics** (C1; outside the tools).
   - The star is at ecliptic latitude −56°, so it is not in the south-ecliptic-pole cap. Visits have 16–36 exposures, and the scan pattern did not change in 2018.
   - I pulled every NEOWISE exposure within 300″ of the star. Twenty-seven field stars with W2 9.5–12.5 changed by +0.006 (W1) and +0.014 (W2) mag across the step, with robust scatter 0.005. None brightened by more than 0.1 mag.
   - Every visit's field zero-point is within ±0.02 mag.
   - The target's −0.17 / −0.36 step is a >30σ outlier.
   - Fainter field stars (W2 ~14.7) show only noise-level excursions.
2. **Blends, moving and new sources** (C2, C3).
   - Relative to the Gaia position propagated with proper motion (22 mas/yr, i.e. 0.2″ over the decade, which is negligible), the WISE centroid moves by 0.013 ± 0.008″ across the step.
   - rchi2 is unchanged, and nb = 1 throughout.
   - Any contaminant must therefore be within ~0.2″.
   - The closest IR neighbours are:
     - an unWISE W1-only source at 7.4″ (5% of the W1 flux);
     - a CatWISE W1 14.7 source at 9.4″;
     - AllWISE sources at 13″ and 16″;
     - a W1 8.75 star at 32″, which sets the halo flag both before and after the step.
   - All of these are flat across 2018.
   - An asteroid would affect one visit, not six years. A comet or transient within 0.2″, steady for six years, is implausible.
   - A background AGN or nuclear transient within 0.2″ would have to rise from undetectable (W2 > 16) to W2 ≈ 12.3 and then hold steady for six years. Over 18 M stars a few chance AGN alignments within 0.2″ are expected, but almost none would brighten by that factor of ~30 into a plateau.
3. **Saturation and nonlinearity.** None. W1 ~11.0 and W2 ~10.9 are 3 mag fainter than saturation. w1sat = w2sat = 0 and ph_qual is AA in all visits.
4. **Stellar explanations** (C5, C6).
   - Dereddened, the star sits on the K3V main sequence (M_G0 ≈ 6.31, (BP−RP)0 ≈ 1.17) with logg 4.58. It is not a pre-main-sequence star with a disk turning on.
   - UVW = (−24, −18, −3) km/s is >12 km/s from Chamaeleon, ε Cha and LCC.
   - Gaia RV from 17 transits is unremarkable, and RUWE is 1.02, so there is no evidence of a close massive companion.
   - Not a Be/shell star (4770 K).
   - Flaring M companion: excluded, because the excess has persisted for six years.
   - A K-dwarf photosphere cannot brighten by 17% at 3.4 µm.
   - Photospheric before the step: AllWISE 2010 matches 2014–17, W1−W3 = 0.17 ± 0.10, and Ks−W1 = 0.06 (C4).
5. **Excess properties** (C4, C5; K15, K16).
   - Onset between 2018 Feb 26 and Aug 8.
   - The first visit after onset is the brightest. The excess then plateaus at T ≈ 1040–1050 K through 2024.
   - Blackbody L_IR/L* ≈ 0.02 at ~0.04 AU. This is extreme for a main-sequence K dwarf, and keeping it up for six years at such small radii needs continuous replenishment.
6. **Optical** (C7, C8).
   - TESS:
     - Sectors S100–S101 are dominated by systematics: ramps and a 0.6-mag five-day offset.
     - The "~11 d" period is not robust (per-sector peaks at 6.6–20 d).
     - The TIC contamination ratio is 3.78. The star supplies only ~21% of the aperture flux, so the "no dips >5%" limit is only ~25% on the star itself.
   - ASAS-SN V:
     - Flat at 13.41 (robust scatter 0.036) through 2014–2018, including Feb–Apr and Jul–Sep 2018.
     - There is a gap in May–June 2018.
     - The photometry is diluted by about 1.6× by the 16″ neighbour and by HD 128641 (V 9.66, F0V) at 32″.
   - SkyMapper on 2018-04-24, inside the onset window: u/v/g/r match 2014 to 0.03 mag.
7. **Novelty** (C9).
   - VarWISE (Paz et al. 2026) already lists the WISE variability: W1/W2 amplitudes 0.18/0.375, classified "lpv". That classification is wrong for a K3V dwarf.
   - The detection of variability is therefore not new. The identification as a newly appeared ~1000 K excess on a main-sequence K dwarf is.
   - Nothing else in SIMBAD, VSX (only Gaia [ROT]) or the literature.
   - Not in the Chamaeleon, ε Cha or LCC membership lists.

## Most plausible explanation

Hot circumstellar dust that appeared abruptly in 2018 and has been resupplied since. The most likely source is a collisional event close to the star (an extreme-debris-disk-like brightening, in the sense of ID8 or ASASSN-21qj), but on an apparently mature K dwarf.

| Explanation | Probability |
|---|---|
| Collisional or debris dust | ~45% |
| Dusty outflow from a star–planet interaction or engulfment (cf. ZTF SLRN-2020; a flash would have to hide in the May–June 2018 ASAS-SN gap) | ~8% |
| Activity or event on an unresolved companion within 0.2″ | ~10% |
| Unrelated background object (AGN etc.) within 0.2″ | ~3% |
| Unexplained or instrumental | ~34% |

The instrumental share is low after the field test. Most of the residual is in "unexplained".

## Wording requirements

- Credit VarWISE (Paz et al. 2026) as the first catalogue of the variability, and note that it misclassifies the star as an LPV.
- Say "an infrared excess appeared". Do not say "the star lit up": there is no evidence the photosphere changed.
- Describe the temperature as "a two-band colour temperature of ~1000 K".
- "K dwarf, likely ≳100 Myr" needs lithium before any age claim.
- Do not state an 11-d rotation period.
- Do not write "TESS rules out dips". TESS is diluted ~5× and starts in 2019.
- No collision claim without spectra or mid-IR data.

## Decisive follow-ups

1. **Close the May–June 2018 optical gap and get a de-blended light curve:**
   - Gaia DR4 epoch photometry (to January 2020; due Dec 2026) resolves the 16″ neighbour;
   - ATLAS-South;
   - ASAS-SN g after 2018 with difference imaging.

   An optical flash means engulfment or merger; dips mean transiting dust; flat light means optically thin dust.
2. **Spectra:**
   - Li 6708 and Hα/Ca II for age and activity;
   - RV epochs for any companion;
   - a near-IR spectrum (or SPHEREx 0.75–5 µm, now public) for the excess shape and CO/H₂O.
3. **Mid-IR** (VISIR, or JWST MIRI): a 10-µm silicate feature would show small, freshly made grains; the 10–25 µm SED gives the dust mass.
4. **Optical monitoring** for ASASSN-21qj-like dips. Prediction: if the dust is orbiting at ~0.04 AU, any transiting structure recurs on ~3–10 d.
